messages.author: 1c3c7aae8066bfc6
messages.subject: Prior specification for Matern parameters
parts:
Hi,

I am new to INLA and I have been impressed by the possibilities that it opens.  I am endeavouring to use it for fitting geostatistical models.

I have run into a (probably small) issue.  Instead of becoming more frustrated, I figure that I should ask people who will know;-)

I am trying to specify prior distributions on the parameters for the Matern function -- I want to use the spatial variance and the matern dependence -- it would be great if I could have a gamma prior for both.  Note that other parameterisations are not all that useful to me.  I understand that this should be done using the inla.spde2.matern() function and the specification of the arguments prior.variance.nominal and prior.kappa.  What is not clear to me is the syntax.  The specification of priors within a INLA f() function or through control.family() and so on, appears to be different (it requires multiple arguments or a list).  Is it different?  Am I being stupid (it wouldn't be the first time)?

I'm also confused about the parameterisation.  I would have naively assumed that the prior I wanted was not implemented.  So, I looked at the `expression' prior.  It mentioned that the scale on which the density of the parameter is the internal scale -- the log scale.  Does this mean that I actually want a log-gamma (which is implemented)?

Just in case you are interested: my goal for doing this is to be able to simulate data from a posterior and analyse (with INLA) using the same model, including priors, used to get the original posterior.  Unfortunately, the original simulation model will have to be, I think, using MCMC as the dependence between the parameters could be important.  If it weren't then I could just simulate from the posterior margins given by INLA.  I don't particularly want to implement an MCMC method, but I may not have much choice.

Any help is appreciated.  Thanks in advance,

Scott

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prior specification for Matern parameters
parts:
Hi,

the spde2 models by default use a multivariate log-normal distribution for the parameters.  However, I think the parameterisation you're asking for is still possible to specify.  You need to construct B.tau and B.kappa in a way that theta1 and theta2 get the desired interpretation, and then specify the prior via control.prior in the f() function to override the default prior model.

Precisely what the B.* matrices need to be depends on which Matern parameterisation you have in mind for the scale/range. If you tell me precisely which one you want I can tell you what B.tau and B.kappa need to be...

As for posterior dependence between the parameters, that _is_ taken into account when evaluating the marginals for the field values, so wether you actually need samples depends, again, on precisely what you are trying to calculate...  That said, you can actually ask inla() to calculate samples with mcmc!

Finn

messages.author: e9fa57e9a1654e87
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prior specification for Matern parameters
parts:
Hi,

Wow, that was quick!  Thanks.

Let's start with the most promising solution, for me.  I didn't know that I could get inla to generate posterior samples.  Great!  This makes my other question(s) obsolete, I think (but see below for my own education).  The next question is: How does one "ask inla() to calculate samples with mcmc"?  In this case I don't really care what the priors are, just as long as they are sensible and suitably vague (but don't give ranges bigger than the world etc).  If all is done in R-INLA, then the between-model consistency issue is automagically solved.  Great again!

As for the prior specification problem -- which I am loosing interest in given the above -- how does this process generate a gamma marginal?  If you start with correlated log-normals and take a transformation of them, then surely the result will be the log-normal multiplied by the jacobian of the transormation?  Of course, it can be approximated by matching up moments/ranges/quantiles(?).  

The parameterisation for the Matern that I am interested in is that given in your JRSS-B paper (equation 1), \sigma^2 and \kappa.  For the MCMC model (from spGLM), these should have gamma as priors.

Thanks again,

Scott

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prior specification for Matern parameters
parts:
On 12/08/13 07:34, Scott Foster wrote:
> Let's start with the most promising solution, for me. I didn't know that
> I could get inla to generate posterior samples. Great! This makes my
> other question(s) obsolete, I think (but see below for my own
> education). The next question is: How does one "ask inla() to calculate
> samples with mcmc"?

The FAQ entry

http://www.r-inla.org/faq#TOC-I-want-to-compare-the-results-from-inla-with-those-obtained-with-MCMC-is-there-any-way-to-do-this-using-inla-

gives an example. Look at the code in the file given by

system.file("demo/Tokyo-compare.R", package="INLA")

for the "magic" parameter you need to specify to get MCMC samples.

> In this case I don't really care what the priors
> are, just as long as they are sensible and suitably vague (but don't
> give ranges bigger than the world etc). If all is done in R-INLA, then
> the between-model consistency issue is automagically solved. Great again!

See the tutorial

http://www.r-inla.org/examples/tutorials/spde-tutorial-from-jss

for how to specify sensible priors when using the default multivariate
normal approach.

> As for the prior specification problem -- which I am loosing interest in
> given the above -- how does this process generate a gamma marginal? If
> you start with correlated log-normals and take a transformation of them,
> then surely the result will be the log-normal multiplied by the jacobian
> of the transormation? Of course, it can be approximated by matching up
> moments/ranges/quantiles(?).

Well, in this case log(sigma^2) and log(kappa) can be used directly in
the specification, so no further transformation is needed.

nu = alpha-dim/2
sigma^2 = gamma(nu)/gamma(alpha)/(4*pi)^nu/kappa^(2*nu)/tau^2

gives

log(tau) =
1/2*log(gamma(nu)/gamma(alpha)/(4*pi)^nu)-log(sigma^2)/2-log(kappa)

so

B.tau = cbind(0.5*log(gamma(nu)/gamma(alpha)/(4*pi)^nu), -1/2, -1)
B.kappa = cbind(0, 0, 1)

gives you the desired parameterisation. You can then get gamma priors
for sigma^2 and kappa by specifying log-gamma for theta1=log(sigma^2)
and theta2=log(kappa), via

f(..., hyper=list(theta1=list(prior="loggamma", param=...),
theta2=list(prior="loggamma", param=...)))

Note that alpha=2 is the default for inla.spde2.matern (i.e. nu=1 for
dim=2), but nu-values between zero and 1 can be approximated by
specifying a fractional alpha-value, in which case the approximation
discussed in the Authors' response to the JRSSB paper discussion is
used. Other nu-values are currently not supported.

Finn

There was some problems with the NAMESPACE in the previous testing
build, but it is fixed now. So if you upgrade it should appear again.

the hyperpar.sample will sample continously wrt the hyperparameters,
wheras the posterior.sample use the integration points used in inla, and
does, as you say, treat the hyperparameters discretely. so if you want
more points, one has to change the integration strategy/parameters in
the inla-call. this purpose of this strategy is computational speed.

Best

H
